_about: The preparation folder's hand-written table of pictures, read by register.py (which writes the subject list, SUBJECTS.json) and pick_subjects.py: each picture's name, file id, role, source, provenance and note (SPEC); the benchmark's fifteen registered again under the one-area sheet rule (RULE_IDS); the owner's working set (TIER1); history, crops' provenance, input ids, rulings, removed pictures, citation keys; the pictures of one ink run (INKPREP_RUN); seed-42 studies made on the Mac (MAC42). Data about the pictures, kept out of the code.
SPEC: Kasha, front view on the dune, watercolour, no ink.

Kasha, head and shoulders against blue sky, in pen and watercolour: the owner's target. Made by an image generator from the owner's photograph (handoff/sources/kasha-portrait-photo.jpg: reference only, never a subject). Added 21 Nov: 'use it as an additional kasha-portrait option'.

The same Kasha portrait in watercolour, no ink: kept as a matched pair with kasha-portrait, to test classification and black fur with and without line. Made by an image generator from the owner's photograph (reference only). Added 21 Nov.
Man, ball and black dog on a beach, watercolour over pen: the painting, not the photograph.
From Sam's photo. Pencil lines visible under the paint.

The Mittens face close-up as a watercolour sketch over visible pencil, no ink, made by an image generator from the owner's photograph (handoff/sources/mittens-closeup-photo.png: reference only, never a subject). A byte copy of handoff/sources/candidates/mittens-closeup-sketch-b.png ('darker pencil, more background', the lead's default; -a and -c are the alternatives: a swap is one copy over this file plus a rerun of its inputs under a new input id). Replaces the 540 px oil frame first used (21 Nov).
AI-generated ink-and-wash image from a public-domain Yale photograph (studio/make-catalog.py).
Made 5 Oct 2026 by a cloud image generator from Sam's photo of Trumbull College. The painted target, not the photograph.
Sterling Memorial Library with the Women's Table, watercolour over ink.
Jean-Honore Fragonard, Rinaldo in the Enchanted Forest, brown wash over chalk on buff paper, public domain.
Francesco Guardi, A Colonnade, Partly Ruined, c. 1780-90, pen and wash, public domain.
Winslow Homer, A Fisherman's Daughter, 1873, watercolour and gouache over graphite, Cleveland Museum of Art 1943.660, CC0 (added by the owner, 21 Nov).

A detail of Winslow Homer, Adirondacks Guide, 1892, watercolour over traces of graphite, AIC 16772, CC0: the guide's head, white beard, hat and shoulders (the owner's pick C2; paint/SET.md:32). Cut once from the whole picture (see cutFrom); the detail is the picture.

A detail of Edouard Manet, Portrait of Berthe Morisot with a Fan, 1874, watercolour over traces of graphite, AIC 1963.812, CC0: head and shoulders (the owner's pick C1; paint/SET.md:31). Cut once from the whole picture (see cutFrom); the detail is the picture.
Rembrandt, a woman reading, pen and wash, public domain. Same bytes as wt/main/examples/targets/rembrandt-woman-reading.jpg.
John Singer Sargent, White Ships, 1908, Brooklyn Museum, public domain. Same bytes as wt/main/examples/targets/white-ships.jpg.

A detail of John Singer Sargent, Venice, c. 1903, watercolour, gouache and graphite, no pen line, Met 50.130.37, CC0: door base, step and canal water (the detail the owner kept of six; paint/SET.md:30). Cut once from the whole picture (see cutFrom); the detail is the picture.

Paul Signac, Boat in Port, c. 1929-31, watercolour over black crayon, Cleveland Museum of Art 2012.26, CC0. The sheet off its mount (paint/SET.md:34); studio/img/signac-boat.jpg is the same work with its mount. Exploratory: the owner, 'add signac for now'; replaces signac-notredame (21 Nov).
G. B. Tiepolo, Bacchus and Ariadne, pen and wash, public domain.

Winslow Homer, The Water Fan, 1898/99, "Watercolor, with blotting and touches of scraping, over graphite, on thick, rough twill-textured, ivory wove paper", Art Institute of Chicago 38666, CC0 (https://www.artic.edu/artworks/38666). Whole sheet, no trim: the museum's full IIIF file, 3000 x 2089 px (studio/img/candidates/hires/homer-water-fan.jpg, same bytes). Inputs made locally on this Mac with the 8-bit MLX model (qwen_local_prep.py), not on a pod. Added 23 Nov (owner). The sheet size here may be re-set once the owner decides the new sheet-size rule (23 Nov).

John Singer Sargent, In Austrian Tyrol, 1911, "watercolor with traces of graphite", Cleveland Museum of Art 1921.1734, CC0 (https://clevelandart.org/art/1921.1734). Whole sheet from the museum's 3400 x 2290 print file (studio/img/candidates/hires/sargent-tyrol.jpg), trimmed only of the white mount: left 28, top 36, right 40 (to x 3360), bottom 24 px (to y 2266), leaving 3332 x 2230. Inputs made locally on this Mac with the 8-bit MLX model, not on a pod. Added 23 Nov (owner). The sheet size here may be re-set once the owner decides the new sheet-size rule (23 Nov).

Winslow Homer, Adirondacks Guide, 1892, the WHOLE painting (the old `homer-guide` is a crop of it and is left as it is): "Transparent watercolor with touches of opaque watercolor, rewetting, blotting and scraping, over traces of graphite, on thick, moderately textured, ivory wove paper", Art Institute of Chicago 16772, CC0. The museum's full file, 3000 x 1831 px, no trim (same bytes as candidates/hires/homer-guide.jpg); real size about 32.9 x 54.5 cm. Has touches of opaque colour (the owner accepts them). Inputs made locally on this Mac with the 8-bit MLX model, not on a pod. Added 23 Nov (owner). The sheet size here may be re-set once the owner decides the new sheet-size rule (23 Nov).

Inputs made locally on this Mac with the 8-bit MLX model, not on a pod. Added 23 Nov (owner). The sheet size here may be re-set once the owner decides the new sheet-size rule (23 Nov).

Prout, Laundresses before the Wasserturm, Nuremberg, National Gallery of Art 70364, "watercolor on wove paper; laid down". Whole sheet, 2902 x 4036 px (portrait); the broken brown line over the washes is brush or pen: the classifier decides its class. Inputs made locally on this Mac with the 8-bit MLX model, not on a pod. Added 23 Nov (owner). The sheet size here may be re-set once the owner decides the new sheet-size rule (23 Nov).

John Singer Sargent, White Ships, 1908, Brooklyn Museum, "Translucent and touches of opaque watercolor and wax resist with graphite underdrawing". The larger file, 1488 x 1057 px (the older 768 x 548 px registration `white-ships` / `sargent-ships` is left as it is, with its inputs, so last night's results keep them). Touches of opaque colour. Inputs made locally on this Mac with the 8-bit MLX model, not on a pod. Added 23 Nov (owner). The sheet size here may be re-set once the owner decides the new sheet-size rule (23 Nov).

Bonington, French Town, Buildings and River, Art Institute of Chicago 30925, "Watercolor on paper", 18.1 x 14.3 cm. Whole sheet, 1664 x 2104 px (portrait; studio/benchmark-set/img/bonington.jpg). No line named by the museum: the classifier decides. Inputs made locally on this Mac with the 8-bit MLX model, not on a pod. Added 23 Nov (owner). The sheet size here may be re-set once the owner decides the new sheet-size rule (23 Nov).
